messages.subject: decimal precision in asymmetry, etc. error outputs
parts:
Andria Dawson on the stan-users' list pointed out this
error message:

> "Error : error in call to eigenvalues_sym; require symmetric matrix,
> but found; x[0,1]=-0.096686:0; x[1,0]=-0.096686:0"

We should print these to the error tolerance we're checking.

Daniel -- can we fix this so when there's an error it prints
up to tolerance of the error checking? I think what we're seeing
here is the default from std::ostream in C++. I think we can just
crank up the error level on the error stream using the stream
method precision():

http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/ios/ios_base/precision/

Or a more nuanced way to do it would be to only reset for tolerance
errors like the above.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: decimal precision in asymmetry, etc. error outputs
parts:
On Tuesday, June 11, 2013 2:35:11 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Andria Dawson on the stan-users' list pointed out this
error message:

 > "Error : error in call to eigenvalues_sym; require symmetric matrix,
 >  but found; x[0,1]=-0.096686:0; x[1,0]=-0.096686:0"

We should print these to the error tolerance we're checking.

It doesn't hurt anything to print the error tolerance. But the error tolerance in that function is 1E-8, so you have to be pretty sloppy to trigger it.

Ben
